scenes.dialogue: Can a High Court end a criminal case before trial? Yes, but only rarely, and never just because the accused calls it false.
Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. When will the High Court quash an F I R or a criminal case, and when will it refuse?
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. When will the High Court quash an FIR or a criminal case, and when will it refuse?

scenes.dialogue: The power sits in Section Five Twenty Eight of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, or B N S S. It succeeds Section Four Eighty Two of the old Code.
scenes.shown: The power sits in Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, or BNSS. It succeeds Section 482 of the old Code.

scenes.dialogue: Nothing in the Sanhita limits the High Court's inherent powers to give effect to orders under it, prevent abuse of process, or secure the ends of justice.
It creates no new power. It preserves a power that belongs to the High Court alone.
What can be quashed? An F I R and its investigation, a charge sheet, a summoning order, or the proceedings themselves.
scenes.shown: What can be quashed? An FIR and its investigation, a charge sheet, a summoning order, or the proceedings themselves.

scenes.dialogue: A charge sheet does not close the door. Anand Kumar Mohatta, under the old Code, says abuse of process may then be aggravated.
Pepsi Foods, also under the old Code, calls summoning an accused a serious matter.
The leading case is State of Haryana versus Bhajan Lal, under the old Code and Article Two Twenty Six. It gives seven illustrative categories.
scenes.shown: The leading case is State of Haryana versus Bhajan Lal, under the old Code and Article 226. It gives seven illustrative categories.

scenes.dialogue: One: the allegations, even taken at face value and accepted in full, make out no offence.
Two: no cognizable offence is disclosed to justify police investigation. Three: the uncontroverted allegations and evidence disclose no offence.
Four: only a non cognizable offence is disclosed, which police cannot investigate without a Magistrate's order.
scenes.shown: Four: only a non-cognizable offence is disclosed, which police cannot investigate without a Magistrate's order.

scenes.dialogue: Five: the allegations are so absurd and inherently improbable that no prudent person could find sufficient ground to proceed.
Six: an express legal bar to the case, or a specific provision giving effective redress.
Seven: the case is manifestly mala fide, or maliciously filed to wreak vengeance out of a private, personal grudge.
The Court stressed that this list is not exhaustive, and that the power must be used very sparingly, with circumspection.
The High Court does not hold a mini trial, or test whether the allegations are true. Disputed defences are left for trial.
scenes.shown: The High Court does not hold a mini-trial, or test whether the allegations are true. Disputed defences are left for trial.
scenes.chip: 5 · WHAT THE HIGH COURT WILL NOT DO

scenes.dialogue: Neeharika Infrastructure, under the old Code, says courts should not thwart investigation. Quashing is the exception, not the rule.
Interim protection must not be routine. An interim stay needs brief reasons, and a no coercive steps order must say what it means.
scenes.shown: Interim protection must not be routine. An interim stay needs brief reasons, and a “no coercive steps” order must say what it means.

scenes.dialogue: Here is a hypothetical. Harish pays Kavya an advance for furniture. Delivery runs late, and he withholds the balance.
scenes.chip: 6 · A BUSINESS DISPUTE WITH A CRIMINAL COLOUR

scenes.dialogue: Instead of suing, Harish files an F I R alleging cheating and forgery. Kavya asks the High Court to quash it.
scenes.shown: Instead of suing, Harish files an FIR alleging cheating and forgery. Kavya asks the High Court to quash it.

scenes.dialogue: Paramjeet Batra, under the old Code, tells the High Court to see whether a civil dispute is given a cloak of criminal offence.
The Supreme Court has also held that a mere breach of contract is not cheating, without dishonest intention at the start.
But a civil dispute can involve a real offence. If the F I R gives specific facts of forgery, the case may proceed.
scenes.shown: But a civil dispute can involve a real offence. If the FIR gives specific facts of forgery, the case may proceed.

scenes.dialogue: Now suppose they settle. Kavya refunds part of the advance, and Harish files an affidavit supporting quashing.
Section Three Fifty Nine lists the offences that can be compounded, some only with the court's permission. Forgery is not among them.
scenes.shown: Section 359 lists the offences that can be compounded, some only with the court's permission. Forgery is not among them.

scenes.dialogue: Gian Singh, under the old Code, holds that the High Court may still quash on settlement, using a power distinct from compounding.
Cases with an overwhelmingly civil flavour, like commercial, matrimonial or family disputes, may be quashed once the parties resolve their entire dispute.
Heinous offences like murder, rape and dacoity affect society, so settlement alone cannot end them, nor Prevention of Corruption Act cases.
Narinder Singh and Parbatbhai Aahir, also under the old Code, add that timing matters, and economic offences affecting the State may not be quashed.
Another route is revision under Sections Four Thirty Eight to Four Forty Two, but not against interlocutory orders.
scenes.shown: Another route is revision under Sections 438 to 442, but not against interlocutory orders.
scenes.chip: 8 · OTHER ROUTES TO THE HIGH COURT

scenes.dialogue: The Supreme Court has also held, under the old Code, that the revision remedy does not, by itself, bar the inherent power.
Quashing petitions are also filed under Article Two Twenty Six. Bhajan Lal's categories cover both powers.
scenes.shown: Quashing petitions are also filed under Article 226. Bhajan Lal's categories cover both powers.

scenes.dialogue: In practice, attach the F I R or charge sheet under challenge, and show which category applies from the prosecution's own papers.
scenes.shown: In practice, attach the FIR or charge sheet under challenge, and show which category applies from the prosecution's own papers.

scenes.dialogue: In a settlement case, file the complainant's affidavit. The State and the complainant are heard, and the court must find the settlement real and complete.
If the petition fails, the case simply continues. That is not a finding of guilt; the trial court still weighs the evidence.
Remember: Section Five Twenty Eight exists to prevent abuse of process. It is used sparingly, and the facts decide.
scenes.shown: Remember: Section 528 exists to prevent abuse of process. It is used sparingly, and the facts decide.

scenes.dialogue: For Kavya, everything turns on what the F I R alleges, and what was truly settled.
scenes.shown: For Kavya, everything turns on what the FIR alleges, and what was truly settled.
